pilots.title: New Mexico Bookkeeping
pilots.description: New Mexico bookkeeping for gross receipts, NTTC evidence, compensating tax, wage withholding and defensible electronic records.
pilots.summary: New Mexico gross receipts tax is imposed on sellers, so the ledger needs receipt classifications and deduction evidence beyond an ordinary sales tax account.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Last reviewed October 16, 2026. Confirm treatment with a qualified professional using current instructions and business facts.

sections.heading: Gross Receipts And Deduction Evidence
paragraphs: New Mexico gross receipts tax is imposed on businesses and may be passed to customers; when passed on, the agency requires it to be separately stated on the invoice. Preserve the activity description and transaction location for the preparer because local location codes affect reporting.

Nontaxable Transaction Certificates relate to specific gross receipts deductions. Keep the certificate type, customer and transaction support together; the agency permits alternative evidence for many deductions but identifies exceptions. Ordinary business expenses do not automatically become gross receipts deductions. Keep net income accounting separate from the tax receipt classification.

sections.heading: Purchase And Vendor Review
paragraphs: New Mexico electronic record rules require detail that supports tax computation and can be interpreted during an examination. Keep supplier identities, item descriptions, amounts, tax information and shipping facts available even where the accounting export uses product or vendor codes.

As a practical accounts payable control, flag purchases requiring compensating tax review and document the preparer decision. Separate goods acquired for resale from items used by the company, and retain the NTTC evidence actually supplied. A certificate used for one type of purchase should not silently carry over to a different activity.

sections.heading: Business Income And Entity Tax Records
paragraphs: New Mexico corporate income and franchise reporting is separate from gross receipts and compensating tax. Federal classification helps determine whether the business uses a corporate, S corporation or other pass through return. Keep tax elections, state activity, ownership and federal return support so the preparer can evaluate both income and franchise obligations rather than assuming the gross receipts filing covers everything.

Maintain a separate rollforward of income and franchise estimates, credits and notices. For a pass through entity, give the preparer member residence, allocation schedules and any applicable owner or entity election documents. The year end reconciliation should connect the final tax adjustments to the financial statements without treating the gross receipts tax base as the same measure as taxable income.

sections.heading: Wage Withholding And Workers Compensation
paragraphs: New Mexico requires covered employers to register and withhold state income tax, with stated exceptions requiring individual facts. Wage withholding uses a separate return from nonwage withholding. Preserve worker instructions, residence, service locations and payroll registers for review.

The agency also collects a workers compensation administration fee for covered employers and employees. Paying that fee does not provide workers compensation insurance, and unemployment reporting is through Workforce Solutions. Reconcile each liability separately rather than treating one payroll provider withdrawal as proof that every employer obligation was completed.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Reports
paragraphs: New Mexico Workforce Solutions requires an activated employer account before accepting wage records and unemployment contributions. Its quarterly contribution report distinguishes total wages, excess wages, taxable wages and tax due. Preserve account activation, assigned rate, employee wage detail and accepted reporting evidence apart from TRD withholding and workers compensation fee records.

Reconcile the unemployment contribution to payroll by employee and quarter, retaining any adjustments to excess wages or coverage. Match the payment and any notice to the Workforce Solutions account rather than a revenue account. Include the outstanding balance and amendment history in the year end payroll handoff so the preparer can distinguish contributions from insurance premiums and the separate administration fee.

sections.heading: Monthly Financial Reporting
paragraphs: Reconcile bank accounts, customer receipts and unpaid vendor bills before presenting financial statements. Maintain a bridge from accounting income to gross receipts reported, showing deductions and adjustments with document references. A low profit month can still contain substantial gross receipts.

Review customer deposits, supplier credits, loan activity and asset purchases with the owner. Keep a separate compensating tax question list and liability schedule. Explain accounting method differences to the preparer rather than changing the reporting method solely to match a cash balance.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Certificate Mismatch
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a New Mexico design business receives a customer certificate but cannot connect its type to the service invoiced. The bookkeeper saves the contract, invoice and certificate and flags the receipt for professional deduction review. The certificate is preserved as evidence without treating its mere existence as a completed tax analysis.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention Scope
paragraphs: Give the preparer reconciled statements, receipts by location and deduction, NTTC support, compensating tax decisions, wage reconciliations, assets and agency notices. Keep electronic code descriptions with transaction exports so the reviewer can reconstruct the reporting bridge.

NMAC 3.1.5.8 states that the Tax Administration Act sets no fixed retention time, while assessment limitations still apply. FYI-105 recommends maintaining the files for ten years because extended assessments can apply, and distinguishes the ordinary assessment period from longer cases. Treat ten years as agency advice, not an invented universal statutory minimum; federal employment, property and special industry records need their own schedules.

pilots.title: North Carolina Bookkeeping
pilots.description: North Carolina bookkeeping for contractor documents, sales and use records, employee certificates and ten year withholding preservation.
pilots.summary: North Carolina contractor and sales files need clear activity evidence, while current employer instructions prescribe a much longer withholding retention schedule.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Last reviewed October 16, 2026. Confirm treatment with a qualified professional using current instructions and business facts.

sections.heading: Sales, Contractors And Transaction Evidence
paragraphs: North Carolina requires retailers, facilitators, real property contractors and consumers to keep records establishing their sales and use tax liability. Retailer records include gross income, gross sales, taxable sales, resale purchases and facilitator transaction information. Keep exemption evidence with the sale it supports.

For construction or repair work, preserve contracts, work descriptions and any applicable capital improvement documentation for professional classification. A contractor label does not settle treatment. Accounts payable should preserve purchase invoices, job use and taxes paid elsewhere so any purchase use tax decision has transaction support.

sections.heading: Employee Certificates And Withholding
paragraphs: The current 2026 employer instructions require North Carolina withholding certificates such as NC-4 and identify payroll reporting duties. Keep signed employee instructions, effective dates, wage registers, amounts withheld, returns and payment confirmations. Work location and residence facts should reach payroll review before state allocations are finalized.

Reconcile periodic payments with the annual NC-3 totals and wage statements. Document corrections in both the payroll system and liability accounts. Unemployment and other employment obligations need their own account checks, and a contractor payment should not be treated as wages or exempt compensation solely from its ledger category.

sections.heading: Business Income And Entity Tax Records
paragraphs: North Carolina corporate income and franchise taxes are separate obligations, and an S corporation return can involve franchise tax even when income ordinarily passes to shareholders. Eligible S corporations and partnerships can elect taxed pass through treatment. Preserve federal classification, state source income, ownership, capital information and any year specific election so the preparer can determine the applicable reporting.

Reconcile corporate or entity estimates, franchise payments and owner related credits in separate schedules. Provide the preparer the tax basis adjustments, state allocation detail and member statements alongside the trial balance. A loss in the profit and loss statement should not be used as evidence that no franchise filing or payment applies, and the preparer should resolve any minimum or special rule from the actual facts.

sections.heading: Vendor Files And Income Classification
paragraphs: A renovation business can receive progress billings, customer advances and owner loans during the same week. Link each receipt to the contract or financing document and preserve changes in scope. The customer ledger should distinguish amounts billed, collected and still disputed.

For vendor bills, keep purchase approval, job delivery and payment together. Separate equipment retained by the company from materials used on a project. Track supplier credits against the original purchase and ask the preparer to resolve uncertain capitalization or tax treatment using the original documentation.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Reports
paragraphs: North Carolina DES uses NCSUITS for quarterly tax and wage reports, contributions and wage adjustments. Covered employer reports identify each employee wages, and continuing businesses must submit a zero report for a quarter without wages. Preserve employer registration, rate notices, accepted wage files and contribution payment confirmations.

Compare quarterly wages with payroll and retain the calculation explaining taxable wages, including relevant wages paid in other states for specialist review. Reconcile DES liabilities independently from NCDOR withholding. At year end, give the preparer the report and adjustment history, contribution balance and status changes; the portal retaining report copies does not replace the business retention schedule.

sections.heading: Monthly Close And Tax Reconciliations
paragraphs: Review project receipts and direct spending alongside customer aging and unpaid suppliers. Reconcile cash, cards and debt, then present a profit and loss statement and balance sheet under the agreed accounting basis. Explain unfinished work and customer advances rather than treating bank deposits as the sole revenue measure.

Maintain distinct sales tax, purchase use tax and withholding schedules. Each should connect opening liability, current activity, adjustments and payments to the filed return. Preserve the reason a transaction was reclassified so a future reviewer can reproduce the result.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Renovation Scope Change
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a North Carolina contractor begins with a repair order and later accepts a broader renovation contract. The bookkeeper retains both scopes, approvals, invoices and project documents and asks the preparer to evaluate the tax treatment of each activity. The example does not classify the entire project from its final invoice title.

sections.heading: Year End And Longer Payroll Preservation
paragraphs: The year end package should contain project revenue detail, sales reconciliations, contractor documents, inventory and asset schedules, debts, annual wage support and unresolved notices. Give the preparer the actual work descriptions behind ambiguous receipts and vendor charges.

The 2026 NC-30 instructions direct retention of withholding records for at least ten years after the last filing of all required reports for the calendar year or the last payment of an amount due for that year, whichever is later. Apply that specific employer instruction rather than a generic three year assumption. Sales, income, federal and property records require separate review, especially where returns or trust tax payments remain unresolved.
